insight.title: Why Small Choices Make Big Decisions Harder
insight.subtitle: How tiny decisions drain the focus you need for important work

sections.text: You spend ten minutes picking a coffee or a font, then feel exhausted when it’s time to sign a contract. Your brain treats every choice as a withdrawal from the same limited account.

This is your decision-making engine at work. It doesn't distinguish between the color of a slide and the direction of a company. Each minor selection adds friction, slowly grinding your judgment to a halt.

By the time you reach high-stakes moments, your clarity is gone. High-performers don't just have better judgment; they have fewer things to judge, preserving their mental energy for the moments that actually matter.
Try this today: When you face a trivial choice today, pick the first decent option in under five seconds.
Quality of thought is determined by the energy you refuse to waste on things that don't matter.

news.title: Apple says it faces world’s largest antitrust fine as India’s regulator hardens stance
news.description: Apple has said that it could potentially be fined a massive $38 billion in an antitrust battle taking place in India after it refused to cooperate with the regulator. Yep, that’s billion with a B. The iPhone maker has persistently refused to submit financial data required by the Competition Commission of India (CCI) after being found guilty of abusing its dominant position in the smartphone market … more…
news.why: Legal fines result in more expensive monthly app store subscriptions.

news.title: Tim Cook to step down as Apple chief as John Ternus named replacement
news.description: Cook, who will stay on as executive chair, praises head of hardware engineering, who will take over on 1 September Apple announced on Monday that it had named a replacement for Tim Cook as CEO after nearly 15 years, with head of hardware engineering John Ternus succeeding him on 1 September. Cook will stay at the company in the role of executive chair. “It has been the greatest privilege of my life to be the CEO of Apple and to have been trusted to lead such an extraordinary company. I love Apple with all of my being,” Cook said in a press release. Continue reading...
news.why: A new leader will change how your future smartphone actually functions.
